metadata.goal: Analyze how the traveler selects routes across repeated trips and identify the trade-offs that appear to shape their route choices.
metadata.dataset_description: Twenty-four repeated-trip summaries and point-level traces expose route frequency, travel-time variability, a midway route switch, and speed–distance trade-offs.

insight_list.insight: Although Route A is not always the fastest option, the traveler repeatedly chooses it across similar trips, and its travel time varies substantially less than the alternatives.

plot.title: Route Choice and Travel-Time Variability
plot.description: Violin and point distributions compare selection frequency and travel-time variability.

insight_list.question: Which route is selected most often across similar trips, and how does its travel-time variability compare with the alternatives?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare route counts and complete travel-time distributions rather than only their means.

insight_list.insight: Most trips follow the same familiar corridor, but this journey switches to a different route midway and reconnects with the habitual route near the destination.

plot.title: Midway Route Switch
plot.description: Repeated Route A traces provide the habitual corridor; the highlighted trip diverges and reconnects.

insight_list.question: Does any trip depart from the habitual corridor midway and reconnect near the destination?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the highlighted point sequence with repeated Route A traces.

insight_list.insight: The selected route is longer than the shorter alternative, but it maintains higher and more stable speeds for most of the trip, resulting in a comparable overall travel time.

plot.title: Distance, Speed Stability, and Travel Time
plot.description: Speed profiles and trip totals compare the selected longer route with the shorter alternative.

insight_list.question: How can the selected route achieve travel time comparable to the shorter alternative despite covering more distance?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare speed level and variability throughout the trip together with total distance and time.

insights: Although Route A is not always the fastest option, the traveler repeatedly chooses it across similar trips, and its travel time varies substantially less than the alternatives.
Most trips follow the same familiar corridor, but this journey switches to a different route midway and reconnects with the habitual route near the destination.
The selected route is longer than the shorter alternative, but it maintains higher and more stable speeds for most of the trip, resulting in a comparable overall travel time.
summary: Across similar trips, Route A is the most frequent and most predictable choice even though alternatives can be faster. One trip temporarily leaves the habitual corridor, and the detailed comparison shows how a longer but faster and steadier route can match the travel time of a shorter alternative.
